[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] Except where noted, evaluations in this section use Petri, the automated adversarial probing harness also used in the automated alignment section above.
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] The way we use Petri deviates from the standard setup in two key ways: 1.
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] We run two judges with different grading bases: Petri’s in-pipeline judge scores severity from a scale of 1 (no violation) to 10 (severe violation) against per-behavior rubrics derived from our taxonomy, and a strict binary judge, which grades against the full requirement definitions across behaviors holistically, cites the offending action and the breached requirements, and produces concrete violation verdicts.
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] We anchor on the binary judge to understand concretely which scenarios do not abide by our behavioral requirements as a whole and rely on Petri’s in-pipeline judge to develop an understanding w.r.t severity of violations within-behavior.
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] We report the mean and max severity score produced by the Petri judge and the overall violation rate determined by our bespoke binary judge.
[meta-muse-spark-1-1-system-card] These scenarios are generated with Petri Bloom (Gupta et al., 2025), an extension of Petri that takes a high-level description of a target behavior and produces a set of scenarios designed to place the model under pressure to violate it.
